temp_level.name: mars_temp_level

support_gate.definition: achieved weight total over expected weight total: the cos(lat)-weighted fraction of the native cells falling in the pixel that carried a usable value
support_gate.thin_support_warning: A pixel passing the coverage gate on a small support fraction is a weak measurement, not a missing one. Filter on support, not on validity alone.

temp_level.source: Mars Climate Database v6.2 web interface, tsurf
temp_level.grid: 64 lon x 48 lat, 3,072 cells for the planet
temp_level.matching_eligible_reason: The MCD output grid is 64 x 48 = 3,072 cells for the whole planet, against 3,145,728 HEALPix pixels at Nside 512 -- 1,024 pixels share every distinct value. At target scale any candidate patch is thermally CONSTANT, so the null test would compare patches that are all thermally identical. This layer is built and stored but must not be used as a matching dimension.
temp_level.resolution_checked: The 64 x 48 output grid IS the GCM grid (model resolution 5.625 x 3.75 deg), so there is no downsampling to undo. The high-resolution flag hrkey=1 was tested against hrkey=0: 3,072 values compared, maximum difference 0.000000 K, zero values differ -- it is ignored for map output. It works only in point mode, which would need 9.3 million HTTP requests for this sampling.
temp_level.gcm_note: MCD is a GCM product. A finer output grid would add the MOLA topographic correction, which is real and large on Mars because surface temperature depends strongly on elevation through pressure -- but it would NOT add 6 km of physical information. A finer grid must never be read as finer knowledge.
temp_level.future_upgrade: TES-derived thermal inertia (Putzig & Mellon, ~3 km) is a MEASURED product at the right scale and is the better source. Logged, not actioned.
temp_level.resampling_note: BIN THEN FILL. Pixels whose footprint contained at least one source cell carry an area-weighted MEAN of those cells. Pixels with no source cell carry a nearest-neighbour COPY and are marked by SUPPORT EXACTLY 0.0 ALONGSIDE A FINITE VALUE -- that combination means copied, not missing. A plate carree source is not uniformly coarse: a 0.5 degree cell is 15.2 km north-south but 15.2*cos(lat) km east-west, so the same source is finer than the pixel near the poles and coarser near the equator. Copying everywhere would have thrown away real polar detail in the lunar target region; binning everywhere would have left most of the sphere empty, which the coverage gate caught at 28.88% valid.
temp_level.tie_note: distinct_levels and largest_tie_fraction are the FOURTH gate. Copied pixels make neighbours carry identical values, and range, coverage and support are all blind to that.
